findings.title: 当社システムへの不正アクセスによる個人情報漏えいの可能性に関するお詫びとお知らせ
findings.summary_md: Nitori Holdings' own disclosure notice, posted on the company's important-notices page under the date November 9, 2026, titled an apology and notice regarding the possible leak of personal information through unauthorized access to a company-managed system. The document is the primary source that the day's coverage quotes: the company states it confirmed unauthorized third-party access on November 6, 2026 and that up to 37.62 million records of personal information held on its servers may have leaked externally. The PDF's embedded creation timestamp is 2026-11-09 18:09 JST (09:09:35Z), and the linked notice is dated November 9, 2026.

findings.title: 【速報】ニトリ 最大3762万件の会員情報が流出の可能性 今月6日不正アクセスを確認 客の氏名、住所、電話番号など流出か カード情報やパスワード含まれず
findings.summary_md: TBS NEWS DIG reported at 17:39 JST on November 9, 2026 that Nitori Holdings had confirmed unauthorized access by a third party to a system it manages on November 6, and that up to about 37.62 million records of member information may have leaked. The report says the affected data includes customer names, addresses and telephone numbers from store and online purchases, and that credit card information and passwords are not included. Nitori warned customers to be wary of suspicious email and telephone calls impersonating the company.

findings.title: ニトリ、不正アクセスにより個人・法人会員の情報最大3762万件が流出の可能性
findings.summary_md: INTERNET Watch reported at 18:23 JST on November 9, 2026 that Nitori Holdings had announced unauthorized access to a system it manages, with up to 37.62 million records on its servers potentially leaked. The affected users are people who ordered through Nitori Net and the official Nitori shops on e-commerce mall sites, with member numbers, names including kana readings, email addresses, addresses, telephone numbers, birth dates and gender in scope for individuals, and company name, department, representative name, company address and telephone, and contact person details in scope for corporate members. The report states that credit card information and login passwords are not included, that the intrusion was detected on November 6 and that access may have continued from mid to late October, and that affected users will be contacted by email or post.
